Title: Insecure Deserialization via XStream in VulnerableComponentsLesson
Analysis:
The `/VulnerableComponents/attack1` endpoint in `VulnerableComponentsLesson` class takes a user-supplied `payload` parameter containing XML data and passes it to `XStream.fromXML(payload)` without configuring any security permissions or sanitization:
```java
    XStream xstream = new XStream();
    xstream.setClassLoader(Contact.class.getClassLoader());
    xstream.alias("contact", ContactImpl.class);
    xstream.ignoreUnknownElements();
...
      contact = (Contact) xstream.fromXML(payload);
```
Unsecure/default configuration of XStream allows arbitrary deserialization / XML injection. An attacker can construct a payload triggering Remote Code Execution (RCE), such as via `java.lang.ProcessBuilder` (CVE-2013-7285), and pass it as the `payload` parameter, which gets executed on the server.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A POST request to `/VulnerableComponents/attack1` with:
- `payload` parameter containing:
```xml
<contact class="java.lang.ProcessBuilder">
  <command>
    <string>sleep</string>
    <string>5</string>
  </command>
  <redirectErrorStream>false</redirectErrorStream>
</contact>
```

Rubric A evaluation:
- Untrusted source: Yes (payload parameter from POST request) (+25)
- Dangerous sink: Yes (`XStream.fromXML`) (+25)
- No sanitization/validation: Yes, no XStream security configuration/allowlist (+25)
- Reachable path: Yes, mapped to `/VulnerableComponents/attack1` (+25)
Total score: 100/100

Title: Insecure Deserialization leading to Remote Code Execution via VulnerableTaskHolder
SQL Injection in ORDER BY clause in Servers.java
Analysis:
The class `Servers` exposes an endpoint mapped to `SqlInjectionMitigations/servers` via `@RequestMapping` and `@GetMapping`.
The method `sort` takes a `column` query/request parameter directly from the user without any sanitization or validation:
`public List<Server> sort(@RequestParam String column) throws Exception`
This parameter is concatenated directly into the SQL query:
```java
      try (var statement =
          connection.prepareStatement(
              "select id, hostname, ip, mac, status, description from SERVERS where status <> 'out"
                  + " of order' order by "
                  + column))
```
Although `PreparedStatement` is used, the column name dynamic concatenation bypasses the parameterized nature because column names and sorting orders cannot be parameterized using standard placeholders.
Since the input `column` is directly concatenated into the ORDER BY clause, an attacker can perform SQL injection (specifically, error-based, boolean-based, or time-based SQL injection via order-by clauses).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A GET request to `/SqlInjectionMitigations/servers?column=(case+when+(true)+then+hostname+else+ip+end)` or a blind SQL injection payload:
`/SqlInjectionMitigations/servers?column=(CASE+WHEN+(SELECT+ASCII(SUBSTR(password,1,1))+FROM+users+WHERE+username='admin')=97+THEN+hostname+ELSE+ip+END)`

Rubric A evaluation:
- Untrusted source: Yes (column request parameter from HTTP GET request) (+25)
- Dangerous sink: Yes (Concatenation into SQL query executed via Statement/PreparedStatement) (+25)
- No sanitization/validation: Yes, absolutely no checks (+25)
- Reachable path: Yes, mapped to `/SqlInjectionMitigations/servers` (+25)
Total score: 100/100

Title: Path Traversal in ProfileUpload via fullName parameter
Analysis:
The `ProfileUpload` class (which extends `ProfileUploadBase`) contains a Path Traversal vulnerability.
Untrusted input is taken from the `fullName` query/form parameter via `@RequestParam(value = "fullName", required = false) String fullName` in the `uploadFileHandler` method of `ProfileUpload`. This input is passed directly to the `execute` method of `ProfileUploadBase`.
In `ProfileUploadBase.execute`, a new file instance is created: `var uploadedFile = new File(uploadDirectory, fullName);` where `uploadDirectory` is `/PathTraversal/<username>`.
Because there is a complete absence of sanitization or validation on `fullName`, an attacker can provide a value containing path traversal sequences (such as `../` or `..\\`) like `../test.png` or `../../test.png`. When `uploadedFile.createNewFile()` and `FileCopyUtils.copy(file.getBytes(), uploadedFile)` are executed, the file will be written outside of the intended target directory, allowing arbitrary file creation/overwrite on the server.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A POST request to `/PathTraversal/profile-upload` with:
- `uploadedFile` multipart form-data parameter containing any file payload
- `fullName` parameter set to `../arbitrary_file.jpg` or `../../arbitrary_file.jpg`

Rubric A evaluation:
- Untrusted source: Yes (fullName parameter from Multipart HTTP POST) (+25)
- Dangerous sink: Yes (File creation / FileCopyUtils.copy) (+25)
- No sanitization/validation: Yes (+25)
- Reachable path: Yes, endpoint is mapped to /PathTraversal/profile-upload (+25)
Total score: 100/100

Title: Bypassable Path Traversal Protection in ProfileUploadFix
Analysis:
The `ProfileUploadFix` class aims to prevent Path Traversal by removing instances of `../` from the user-provided `fullName` parameter.
The input is sanitized using: `fullName != null ? fullName.replace("../", "") : ""`
However, this sanitization is insufficient and can be bypassed. The `replace()` function is not recursive and does not run in a loop.
If an attacker provides a nested traversal sequence such as `..././` or `....//`, the replacement of `../` on `....//` (which is `..` + `../` + `/`) will remove the middle `../`, leaving `../` intact.
Specifically, `..././` will become `../` after replacement, and `....//` will become `../` after replacement.
The resulting string containing the traversal sequence is passed to `super.execute()`, which will create a file relative to `uploadDirectory` using the traversed path, leading to path traversal.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A POST request to `/PathTraversal/profile-upload-fix` with:
- `uploadedFileFix` multipart form-data parameter containing a file
- `fullNameFix` parameter set to `....//test.jpg` which gets sanitized to `../test.jpg` and writes the file to the parent directory.

Rubric A evaluation:
- Untrusted source: Yes (fullNameFix parameter from HTTP POST) (+25)
- Dangerous sink: Yes (File creation / FileCopyUtils.copy) (+25)
- Insufficient/Bypassable sanitization: Yes, single non-recursive replace of "../" (+25)
- Reachable path: Yes, mapped to /PathTraversal/profile-upload-fix (+25)
Total score: 100/100
